reason: The spool is turned and six-fold symmetric about its axis (a six-hole circle at 60° pitch on one end, twelve-hole circles at 30° on both flanges). The anchors distinctive enough to align by all lie on the axis; the off-axis repeats (holes, chamfers and their faces) then vote for the turn about it, and six turns fit them equally (alignment.fold 6, symmetric set). Which copy is which is undetermined by the geometry, so, as for any symmetric part, the turn giving the motion nearest the identity is taken and every off-axis feature and face is carried, consistently, onto its image under that turn: here a 30° turn rather than the motion's own, so the 42 off-axis features and 72 faces land on their symmetric copies. Under translate, rot_x90 and rot_y180 the identity-nearest turn is the motion's own and everything is carried to itself.

Kernel surface recovery (recover.rs) is not motion invariant here: a B-spline face next to the boss and a turned step is recovered as a plane in the unmoved part and not in this placement, so its type in the two features' neighbourhoods (and in its neighbours' adjacency) changes from plane to bspline. The features are still matched to themselves, as adapted. The fix belongs in recover.rs (a placement-independent fit tolerance).

The pole handling in boundary_nodes/curve_cuts is the likely place (not yet confirmed). (2) B-spline quadrature as for cgb207: B-spline faces matched to themselves but reported adapted (area, normal). Here: sphere faces 240, 268 and 276 come out orphaned (their areas no longer match anything), and B-spline faces 37 and 762 adapted.

The recogniser's rounding, not correspondence, is at fault; Python behaves the same.
